messages.author: 6e3bf202055f2791
messages.subject: sem plot without indicators
parts:
Dear all, does anyone know how I can use semTools or semPlot (or any other package) to create a path diagram without indicators? (it looks too cluttered with all indicators)
Thank you for your time

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: sem plot without indicators
parts: Dear all, does anyone know how I can use semTools or semPlot (or any other package) to create a path diagram without indicators?

You can post to the developer's forum to ask him (Sacha):  http://sachaepskamp.com/forums

You could also fit the CFA, save the common-factor covariance matrix, then fit the structural model to that.  Using semPlot would generate the plot you want because no indicators would be in the model, but the latent variables would be depicted with rectangles instead of circles... Perhaps if semPlot can't exclude the measurement model, there is still a way to choose the shape for your observed variables, so the ad hoc solution would work to make the Step-2 variables look like latents.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: sem plot without indicators
parts: I also have a logistic regression as part of the mode, do you think I could/should include this in the plot as well using the trick with the common-factor covariance matrix?

I'm not sure if (or how) semPlot depicts nonlinear relations, so that would also be something to ask Sacha on his forum.  My guess is that with something that nuanced, you might be better off making your own path diagram using the Insert --> Shapes feature in Microsoft Word/PPT.
